The Company Is Known As Dragons of Hell

One hundred ten Soldiers trained and certified to enter the hot zone with confidence. Who We Are

Mission & Vision

Why the 44th exists, and the standard the company holds itself to — every formation, every mission, every day.

Mission Statement
The 44th Chemical Company (Hazard Response) conducts CBRN reconnaissance, surveillance, and decontamination operations in support of the 22d Chemical Battalion and the 48th Chemical Brigade — and, as part of the Defense CBRN Response Force, stands ready to deploy in support of civil authorities to save lives, protect the force, and mitigate the effects of CBRN incidents at home and abroad.

44th Chemical Company · Fort Bliss, TX

Vision Statement
The most trusted hazard response company in the brigade: a disciplined team of 110 technical experts, trained and certified to enter the hot zone with confidence — ready at a moment's notice, lethal to no one, lifesaving to everyone. One team, one standard: no fail.

One Team · One Standard · No Fail

Trained for the Hot Zone — Ready at a Moment's Notice

Dragons of Hell

That is the name the company answers to — and it is earned at formation. The call-and-response is a unit tradition: the commander brings the company to attention, and the Dragons answer loud enough for the whole battalion to hear.

What We Do

Our Missions

Two standing commitments define the 44th: defending the homeland as part of the Defense CBRN Response Force, and proving readiness in the field, exercise after exercise.

DCRF

Defense CBRN Response Force

As part of the Defense CBRN Response Force, the 44th stands ready to deploy inside the United States in support of civil authorities after a CBRN incident — working alongside local, state, and federal responders when minutes matter most.

  • CBRN reconnaissance — identifying and marking contaminated areas so responders can work safely.
  • Mass-casualty decontamination — processing casualties and responders through the decon line, fast and by the standard.
  • Search & extraction support — assisting urban search and rescue teams operating in contaminated environments.
  • Support to civil authorities — integrating with civilian incident command under Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA).

FTX

Field Training Exercises

Field training exercises take the company out of the motor pool and into realistic, evaluated lanes — validating that every platoon and squad can perform its collective CBRN tasks to standard, day or night, in full protective posture.

  • Reconnaissance lanes — mounted and dismounted CBRN recon validated against live training scenarios.
  • Detailed equipment decontamination — full DED operations for vehicles and equipment, to the technical standard.
  • Collective task validation — platoon and squad CBRN tasks evaluated as a team, not on paper.
  • Sustained operations — operating in MOPP posture over extended field problems, including night operations.

How We Prepare

Training Programs

Readiness is built on a training calendar that never really stops — individual skills, crew drills, and certifications layered week after week.

PROGRAM — 01

CBRN Defense Training

The foundation: protective mask and MOPP gear proficiency, detection equipment, contamination avoidance, and immediate-action drills every Soldier in the company maintains.

PROGRAM — 02

Detailed Equipment Decon (DED)

Hands-on mastery of the detailed equipment decontamination line — stations, throughput, and quality control that return vehicles and equipment to the fight, certified clean.

PROGRAM — 03

Platoon & Squad Certifications

Collective certification gates that prove each squad and platoon can execute its mission-essential tasks together — reconnaissance, surveillance, and decontamination — to standard.

PROGRAM — 04

Leader Development

Leader professional development for NCOs and officers: troop-leading procedures, risk management, and the technical depth that turns 74D specialists into CBRN leaders.
